components.note: Sigma-algebra (also sigma-field, preserving the Durrett term), countable includes finite, empty union/intersection conventions, algebra of sets, sigma(C) with nonempty defining family.
Empty set, countable intersections, differences, arbitrary intersections of sigma-algebras, minimality/uniqueness of sigma(C); proved.
Worked countercase: finite-cofinite algebra is not a sigma-algebra; generated sigma-algebra identified.
Nonnegative extended sums by suprema, no infinity subtraction, measure, countable additivity, finite/probability measure, probability space, null, almost surely.

Finite additivity incl. empty family, monotonicity, finite difference formula, countable subadditivity, null unions, continuity from below/above with finiteness premise, probability consequences; proved.

Grouping of nonnegative sums incl. infinite values and empty blocks, atomic measure construction, converse uniqueness; proved; remark 149-155 limits it to nonnegative series and links the finite models.
Worked countable model: normalization, decreasing tails with empty intersection, continuity from above and below, parity probabilities.
Worked boundary: counting measure breaks continuity from above; no uniform mass on N+; finitely additive 0-1 assignment with no countably additive extension.
Euclidean open sets, Borel sigma-algebra generated by them, one-dimensional notation.
Rational rectangles in R^d, rational rays and real rays in R; proved with both inclusions.
Inverse image (not invertibility), measurability, random element/variable/vector, notation, sigma(X).
Generator criterion, rational-ray criterion, sigma(X) minimal and generated by inverse generators, inclusion in F; proved.
Worked case: sigma(Y) of parity listed; X not sigma(Y)-measurable; sub-sigma-algebra introduced.
Indicator, simple function, equivalent representation (proved under C015), non-disjoint sets allowed, empty sum.
Composition, coordinatewise criterion (both directions), continuity implies Borel measurability, sums/products/abs/max/min, indicators, simple-function equivalence; proved.
Extended reals with generating rays, sup/inf of the empty set, liminf/limsup, almost sure convergence.

inf/sup/liminf/limsup measurable, finite pointwise limit measurable, convergence event measurable, dyadic simple approximation incl. Z=infinity with monotonicity cases; proved; boundary remark 348-352.
Law/distribution (Durrett term preserved), pushforward, point mass, same law across spaces.
Law is a probability measure, composition formula, atomic-source sum, countable-target sum and normalization for any source; proved; worked laws 392-398.
Pi-system and lambda-system (nested differences, increasing unions).
Pi-lambda theorem and uniqueness of probability measures agreeing on a generating pi-system; proved incl. empty pi-system.

components.gap: Definition text (417-425) supplies F_X, the left limit and right continuity, but the identified source variant is not preserved: the held Durrett source at the cited extent (secs. 1.1-1.3, line 14) names this object the "distribution function" (PTE5 printed p.10: "its distribution function, F(x) = P(X <= x)"; Thms 1.2.1-1.2.2 p.11), while the handbook calls it the "cumulative distribution function" with no note of Durrett's term. On the same route the finite chapter (finite-probability.tex 51-53) records that Grinstead-Snell use "distribution function" for the mass function and that it does not mean a cumulative distribution function; Durrett's opposite use of the same name is recorded nowhere on the route. Needed: a sentence at def:p15-cumulative-distribution recording that Durrett calls F_X the distribution function.

components.note: Monotone, [0,1], right continuity, endpoint limits, interval/left-limit/jump formulas, discontinuities = atoms and at most countable, CDF determines law; proved. Matches Durrett Thm 1.2.1 (i)-(v) (held PDF printed pp.10-11).
Worked CDF of the waiting law with jumps equal to point masses; discrete distribution defined.

Boundary: Borel space is not a measure; CDF existence converse needs a measure construction; Durrett Thm 1.2.2 (printed p.11) uses Lebesgue measure on (0,1), and Thms 1.1.4/1.1.9 with App. A.1 construct it - verified in held PDF (pdf pp.11, 13, 19, 463-464); uniqueness supplies no existence; forward references resolve to existing labels sec:p15-integration-expectation, sec:p15-radon-nikodym, sec:p15-conditional-expectation, sec:p15-regular-conditional-laws.
